handshake.instructions:
This agent monitors a Venus lending position on BNB Chain,
stress-tests it against collateral price falls, and repays the minimum amount
needed to restore a safe health factor before liquidation.

Health factor = (collateral value x each market's liquidation threshold) / debt
value. Liquidation becomes possible at 1.0. Bands: SAFE above 1.50, WARNING 1.20
to 1.50, CRITICAL at or below 1.20.

An account can hold positions in several Venus pools — Core and the Isolated
Pools — and they are SEPARATE RISK SILOS. Collateral in one does not back a borrow
in another, so health factors are per pool and never blended; `get_pools` shows
them all. Only the Core pool is actionable by this agent.

Two risk levels are reported and they mean different things. `risk` is the band
of the CURRENT health factor. `effective_risk` also accounts for the stress test,
so a position that is WARNING now but CRITICAL after a routine 15% fall reports
CRITICAL there. Only `risk` can trigger automatic action.

Every tool here is read-only, except `pause`. You CANNOT execute a protection
through this interface — `simulate_protection` shows what the agent would do, and
only a human can make it do it.

You can read ANY address with the `account` argument. The agent can only PROTECT
the position it holds the keys for; `get_status` reports that as `protectable`.

Useful order: `get_status` for the current picture, `get_stress_test` for what a
price fall would do, `simulate_protection` for the repayment that would be needed
and where it would come from.

declared.name: get_status
declared.description:
Current picture: health factor, risk band, stress curve and whether the
    agent can protect this position. Reads any address.

declared.name: get_metadata
declared.description: What this agent is, which protocols it supports, and its on-chain identity.

declared.name: get_strategy
declared.description:
The declared strategy, the health-factor thresholds, the funding order and
    the risk controls currently in force.

declared.name: get_position
declared.description:
Every Venus market the account touches, priced and weighted.

    Includes markets outside this agent's registry: they count toward the health
    factor and are reported with ``actionable: false``, meaning the agent can see
    them but cannot redeem or repay them.

declared.name: get_pools
declared.description:
Every Venus pool the account touches, assessed SEPARATELY.

    Venus Core and each Isolated Pool are separate risk silos: collateral in one
    does not back a borrow in another, so an account can be comfortably safe in one
    pool and be liquidated in another. There is deliberately no blended health
    factor — an average would hide exactly the pool that matters.

    Only the Core pool is actionable by this agent; each row says so.

declared.name: get_risk
declared.description:
Health factor, liquidation price, distance to liquidation, and the
    repayment that would restore a safe level.

declared.name: get_stress_test
declared.description:
What a collateral price fall would do to the health factor.

    The forward-looking half of the agent: at which simulated drop the position
    becomes CRITICAL, and at which it becomes liquidatable.

declared.name: get_performance
declared.description: Protection counts, gas spent, and the rolling 24-hour realised cost.

declared.name: get_transactions
declared.description: The audit trail (spec section 19), newest first.

declared.name: get_chain_info
declared.description:
Network, block height, gas price, BNB price, and how far the Venus oracle
    and PancakeSwap spot disagree.

declared.name: monitor_now
declared.description:
Re-read the position from chain and re-assess it right now.

    Changes no position and signs nothing.

    REQUIRES AN API KEY — it is a dozen chain reads per call, and the result is
    readable afterwards through the unauthenticated read tools.

declared.name: simulate_protection
declared.description:
Show what protecting this position WOULD do, without executing.

    Equivalent to ``POST /protect?dry_run=true``. This is the closest a model can
    get to protecting: it can ask what the agent WOULD do, never make it do it.

    REQUIRES AN API KEY — it prices swap routes against live pools, which costs
    both time and RPC.

declared.name: pause
declared.description:
Emergency stop. Refuses all further swaps and repayments; monitoring
    continues.

    The only state-changing tool exposed, and exposed with a caveat worth stating
    plainly. In a TRADING agent, pausing is unambiguously fail-safe: the worst a
    hostile prompt achieves is a trade that does not happen. In a GUARDIAN it is
    not — pausing stops a liquidation rescue, so a prompt-injected pause has a
    real cost.

    It is exposed because an operator driving the agent from an LLM host needs a
    stop button, and it is the direction a human can always reverse. There is
    deliberately no matching ``activate``: resuming is a decision for a person,
    not for a model reading untrusted text.

    REQUIRES AN API KEY.
